title: Direct OpenCode HTTP Execution Path Decision
claim: ForgePilot MCP should treat the remote runner as legacy optional infrastructure for now; the preferred near-term path for OpenCode model lifecycle work is the direct OpenCode HTTP API from the MCP bridge, with runner-start no longer required for the first HTTP-based model runs.
summary: FP-MCP-287 records the operator decision to keep the remote runner available for legacy/optional purposes while proceeding on the direct OpenCode HTTP lifecycle path. This checkpoint does not refactor server.ts, does not start OpenCode, does not contact the runner start endpoint, does not consume approval, and does not authorize model execution. It exists to mark the architectural pivot before preparing direct-HTTP lifecycle/model-run work.
caveats: The remote runner is not deleted and remains useful as a future isolated execution-plane abstraction.
Existing guarded-runner artifacts remain historical evidence and should not be rewritten.
FP-MCP-276 remains a runner-shaped preparation packet and should not be reused as authority for broad server.ts refactoring.
A future implementation packet should make any code-level deprecation marker explicit in relevant docs or server capability metadata.

structuredRecord.nextWork: prepare direct HTTP lifecycle path toward model-assisted MCP server.ts refactoring
structuredRecord.supersededCriticalPath: runner-start is no longer required for initial OpenCode HTTP lifecycle execution

observedResult: ForgePilot MCP should treat the remote runner as legacy optional infrastructure for now; the preferred near-term path for OpenCode model lifecycle work is the direct OpenCode HTTP API from the MCP bridge, with runner-start no longer required for the first HTTP-based model runs.
